tb.name: Trouble Brewing
tb.theme: A clean Demon hunt complicated by poisoning, drunkenness, registration, and role bluffs.

bmr.name: Bad Moon Rising
bmr.theme: Death is evidence: survival, extra deaths, no-death nights, and protection must be tested carefully.

snv.name: Sects & Violets
snv.theme: Dense information, character changes, madness, and Demon-specific world rules.

grimm.name: A Grimm Chorus
grimm.theme: Variable deaths and delayed threats built around Summoner, Yaggababble, Ojo, Po, and Pukka.

roles.name: Amnesiac
roles.ability: You do not know what your ability is. Each day, privately guess what it is: you learn how accurate you are.
roles.firstNightReminder: Do whatever needs to be done to satisfy the Amnesiac's ability.
roles.otherNightReminder: Do whatever needs to be done to satisfy the Amnesiac's ability.
roles.play: Keep a precise log of triggers, choices, outcomes, and the Storyteller's warmth scale. Guess the mechanism in layers instead of naming an over-specific final ability immediately.
roles.bluff: Invent a simple hidden ability with observable triggers, then ask the Storyteller plausible guesses. Overly elaborate fake mechanisms are difficult to sustain.
roles.story: Design a concise, discoverable ability before setup. Record exact triggers and use a consistent warmth scale for daily guesses.

roles.name: Apprentice
roles.ability: On your 1st night, you gain a Townsfolk ability (if good), or a Minion ability (if evil).
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the *YOU ARE* info token, then a Townsfolk or Minion token. Swap the Apprentice & Townsfolk or Minion tokens. :reminder:
roles.play: Identify how your granted ability changes the setup and use it immediately if appropriate. Your alignment is public, so the hidden information lies in the ability and its use.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Artist
roles.ability: Once per game, during the day, privately ask the Storyteller any yes/no question.
roles.play: Ask a yes/no question whose answer separates broad world families. Confirm wording with the Storyteller before committing your once-per-game ability.
roles.bluff: Use a question that sounds efficient and report the answer town expects to hear. State the exact yes/no wording so it can be evaluated.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Assassin
roles.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a player: they die, even if for some reason they could not.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Assassin might choose a player. :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Hold the unstoppable kill for a protected target, a Professor candidate, or a moment when the extra death can be misattributed. Using it too early may reveal the Minion set.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Barber
roles.ability: If you died today or tonight, the Demon may choose 2 players (not another Demon) to swap characters.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Barber died today or tonight, show the Demon the *THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU* & Barber tokens. If the Demon chose 2 players, wake one at a time. Show the *YOU ARE* token & their new character token.
roles.play: Announce your death clearly and track whether role claims change afterward. The Demon may swap two players, so preserve pre-death information and identities.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Barista
roles.ability: Each night, until dusk, 1) a player becomes sober, healthy & gets true info, or 2) their ability works twice. They learn which.
roles.firstNightReminder: Choose a player. Wake them, show the *THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU* & Barista tokens, then give a finger signal. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: Choose a player. Wake them, show the *THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU* & Barista tokens, then give a finger signal. :reminder:
roles.play: The Storyteller's boost is powerful but intentionally flexible. Tell the group exactly what you were told, then check whether duplication or sobriety altered an ability.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Baron
roles.ability: There are extra Outsiders in play. [+2 Outsiders]
roles.play: The setup impact is already spent, so you may take social risks. Support an Outsider-count world, bluff a plausible Townsfolk, or absorb an execution that protects the Imp.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Beggar
roles.ability: You must use a vote token to vote. If a dead player gives you theirs, you learn their alignment. You are sober & healthy.
roles.play: Ask dead players strategically for vote tokens and use the alignment information to build a public or private trust chain. Preserve enough voting power for the final days.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Bishop
roles.ability: Only the Storyteller can nominate. At least 1 opposing player must be nominated each day.
roles.play: Use Storyteller-selected nominees as information, but remember the Storyteller may balance rather than identify evil. Keep the town from treating every nomination as a hard ping.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Bone Collector
roles.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a dead player: they regain their ability until dusk.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Bone Collector might choose a dead player. :reminder: If necessary, wake the chosen player to use their ability.
roles.play: Return a dead ability at the moment it can change the game, and confirm that the player understands the one-night window.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Bureaucrat
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself): their vote counts as 3 votes tomorrow.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Bureaucrat chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Bureaucrat chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Give triple voting power to a player whose intentions you can read. Announce the arithmetic clearly and avoid accidentally handing evil control of the block.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Butcher
roles.ability: Each day, after the 1st execution, you may nominate again.
roles.play: Use the extra nomination after an execution only when it improves your team's position. Do not let the day continue indefinitely without a clear second case.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Butler
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself): tomorrow, you may only vote if they are voting too.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Butler chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Butler chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Choose a master likely to vote and make your legal votes visible. Your behavior can become social evidence, but the ability itself does not confirm either alignment.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Cannibal
roles.ability: You have the ability of the recently killed executee. If they are evil, you are poisoned until a good player dies by execution.
roles.play: Track each executed player's claimed role and what ability you should now have. Evil executees poison you, so suspicious results can themselves locate an evil death.
roles.bluff: Track executees and claim the appropriate inherited ability. After an evil execution, poisoned-looking information gives you useful cover.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Cerenovus
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player & a good character: they are “mad” they are this character tomorrow, or might be executed.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Cerenovus chooses a player & a character. :reminder: Put the Cerenovus to sleep. Wake the target. Show the *THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU* token, the Cerenovus token, then the madness-character token.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Cerenovus chooses a player & a character. :reminder: Put the Cerenovus to sleep. Wake the target. Show the *THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU* token, the Cerenovus token, then the madness-character token.
roles.play: Choose a madness claim that disrupts information and creates double claims. Coordinate with evil so the target's forced story supports a larger false world.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Chambermaid
roles.ability: Each night, choose 2 alive players (not yourself): you learn how many woke tonight due to their ability.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Chambermaid chooses 2 living players. Give a finger signal.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Chambermaid chooses 2 living players. Give a finger signal.
roles.play: Choose two living players with different expected wake patterns. Record the pair and number; repeated checks can expose bluffs, drunkenness, or Demon identity.
roles.bluff: Build numbers from who truly wakes on the script. Include yourself only when legal and avoid impossible repeated patterns.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Chef
roles.ability: You start knowing how many pairs of evil players there are.
roles.firstNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.play: Draw the seating circle and test every evil arrangement against your number. Your information usually becomes stronger after alignments or Minions are narrowed down.
roles.bluff: Choose a number that fits at least two evil seating worlds and be ready to draw them. A low number is easier to maintain than a dramatic unsupported high one.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Clockmaker
roles.ability: You start knowing how many steps from the Demon to its nearest Minion.
roles.firstNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.play: Count steps both directions around the seating circle and list every Demon–Minion arrangement that matches. Revisit the number after character changes or Vortox suspicion.
roles.bluff: Choose a number that fits the actual evil spacing but also points to alternate pairs. Be ready to update after Pit-Hag or Snake Charmer changes.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Courtier
roles.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a character: they are drunk for 3 nights & 3 days.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Courtier might choose a character. :reminder: :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Courtier might choose a character. :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Choose a high-impact character when timing is valuable, often after evidence points to a Demon or dangerous Minion. Record the three-night window exactly.
roles.bluff: Claim a drunk target and a precise three-night window that explains events. Pick a character whose apparent malfunction has already occurred.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Damsel
roles.ability: All Minions know a Damsel is in play. If a Minion publicly guesses you (once), your team loses.
roles.firstNightReminder: During Minion Info, show the Minions the Damsel token. If you haven't done this yet, do so now. If the Damsel was chosen by the Huntsman, show the *YOU ARE* info token & their new character token.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Damsel was chosen by the Huntsman, show the *YOU ARE* info token & their new character token.
roles.play: Hide among plausible Townsfolk claims and avoid a role story that Minions can eliminate quickly. Coordinate a broad Damsel-protection strategy without identifying yourself.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Deviant
roles.ability: If you were funny today, you cannot die by exile.
roles.play: Use humor and social pressure to make exile a real decision without derailing the game. Your alignment should affect how much chaos you create.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Devil's Advocate
roles.ability: Each night, choose a living player (different to last night): if executed tomorrow, they don't die.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Devil's Advocate chooses a living player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Devil's Advocate chooses a living player. :reminder:
roles.play: Protect the Demon or frame a good player by alternating targets legally. Plan around executions so survival supports the world evil wants town to believe.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Dreamer
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself or Travellers): you learn 1 good & 1 evil character, 1 of which is correct.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Dreamer points to a player. Show 1 good & 1 evil character token, 1 of which is their character.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Dreamer points to a player. Show 1 good & 1 evil character token, 1 of which is their character.
roles.play: Choose players who can be challenged privately and track both characters shown. Exact repeated role stories can expose evil, but poisoning and No Dashii proximity matter.
roles.bluff: For each target, name one real claimed good character and one evil character. Preserve the exact pairings in a ledger.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Drunk
roles.ability: You do not know you are the Drunk. You think you are a Townsfolk character, but you are not.
roles.play: Play the Townsfolk token you saw honestly. If contradictions accumulate, test a Drunk world without automatically inverting every result—unreliable information can still be true.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Choose the believed Townsfolk before bag draw and place both tokens correctly. Simulate all wake-ups; give information that damages good without instantly proving drunkenness.

roles.name: Empath
roles.ability: Each night, you learn how many of your 2 alive neighbors are evil.
roles.firstNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.otherNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.play: Track both neighbors every night and record exactly when the number changes. Consider deaths, seating changes, poisoning, and Recluse registration before accusing either side.
roles.bluff: Change numbers only when deaths or seating justify it, and decide in advance whether your lie frames one neighbor or creates a poison story.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Evil Twin
roles.ability: You & an opposing player know each other. If the good player is executed, evil wins. Good can't win if you both live.
roles.firstNightReminder: Wake both twins. Allow eye contact. Show the good twin's character token to the Evil Twin & vice versa.
roles.play: Build a complete good-role story and attack your twin's credibility without making the pair mechanically trivial. Evil wins socially if town cannot safely choose between you.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Exorcist
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player (different to last night): the Demon, if chosen, learns who you are then doesn't wake tonight.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Exorcist chooses a player. :reminder: Put the Exorcist to sleep. If the Exorcist chose the Demon: Wake the Demon. Show the *THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU* & Exorcist tokens. Point to the Exorcist.
roles.play: Rotate through Demon candidates and watch for a matching no-death night. Once you hit, the Demon learns you, so decide whether to reveal immediately or use the pressure quietly.
roles.bluff: Claim choices that align with no-death nights, then accuse the chosen player. Remember you cannot choose the same player on consecutive nights.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Fang Gu
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. The 1st Outsider this kills becomes an evil Fang Gu & you die instead. [+1 Outsider]
roles.otherNightReminder: The Fang Gu chooses a player. :reminder: If they chose an Outsider (once only): Replace the Outsider token with the spare Fang Gu token. Put the Fang Gu to sleep. Wake the target. Show the *YOU ARE* and Fang Gu tokens & give a thumbs-down. :reminder:
roles.play: Find and kill an Outsider when the jump creates a better Demon. Afterward, the new evil player must understand the existing evil team and outsider-count world.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Give Demon information and three legal bluffs, process protection and poisoning before deaths, and check victory conditions after every death or character change.

roles.name: Fisherman
roles.ability: Once per game, during the day, visit the Storyteller for some advice to help your team win.
roles.play: Wait until the game has enough structure for specific advice, but not so long that you die unused. Record the Storyteller's exact words and ask what action they imply.
roles.bluff: Quote advice that recommends a concrete but defensible action. Avoid advice that amounts to the Storyteller simply naming the Demon.
roles.story: Give actionable advice that helps the player's team in the current position. It may be indirect, but it should not be a riddle with no practical reading.

roles.name: Flowergirl
roles.ability: Each night*, you learn if a Demon voted today.
roles.otherNightReminder: Either nod or shake your head.
roles.play: Track exactly who voted each day and compare with the nightly yes/no. Dead Demon votes, Vortox, poisoning, and Demon changes all affect interpretation.
roles.bluff: Track Demon voting privately and give a result that supports your chosen suspect set. The public vote record must remain compatible.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Fool
roles.ability: The 1st time you die, you don't.
roles.play: Spend your extra life to test executions or absorb danger, but remember Assassin bypasses protection and drunkenness removes the safety net.
roles.bluff: Volunteer for execution and rely on evil protection only if coordinated. Otherwise keep the extra life untested and claim Assassin or drunkenness if necessary.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Fortune Teller
roles.ability: Each night, choose 2 players: you learn if either is a Demon. There is a good player that registers as a Demon to you.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Fortune Teller chooses 2 players. Nod if either is the Demon (or the *RED HERRING*).
roles.otherNightReminder: The Fortune Teller chooses 2 players. Nod if either is the Demon (or the *RED HERRING*).
roles.play: Choose pairs that split candidate worlds rather than repeatedly checking the same suspect. Build around the red herring and hide early if your checks are producing useful exclusions.
roles.bluff: Keep a written fake choice history including a red-herring explanation. Mix yes and no results instead of steering every check directly at good players.
roles.story: Mark one good red herring. A sober check is yes if either selected player is the Demon or red herring, subject to registration.

roles.name: Gambler
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player & guess their character: if you guess wrong, you die.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Gambler chooses a player & a character. :reminder:
roles.play: Make guesses with a reason and keep a private ledger. A death supports a wrong guess but may have other causes; surviving does not confirm the player if protection or drunkenness is possible.
roles.bluff: Publish nightly character guesses and make your survival plausible. Coordinate with deaths so a wrong guess never appears to have been consequence-free without explanation.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: General
roles.ability: Each night, you learn which alignment the Storyteller believes is winning: good, evil, or neither.
roles.firstNightReminder: Give a thumb signal.
roles.otherNightReminder: Give a thumb signal.
roles.play: Treat the result as the Storyteller's current evaluation, not a mechanical alignment count. Ask what changed since yesterday—votes, trust, surviving roles, and remaining win conditions.
roles.bluff: Report a trend rather than a suspiciously precise verdict. Tie changes to visible game events so the Storyteller-opinion claim feels grounded.
roles.story: Evaluate the actual chance of each team winning, including social position and abilities, then answer consistently. The result is opinion, not permission to randomize.

roles.name: Godfather
roles.ability: You start knowing which Outsiders are in play. If 1 died today, choose a player tonight: they die. [-1 or +1 Outsider]
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the character tokens of all in-play Outsiders.
roles.otherNightReminder: If an Outsider died today, the Godfather chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Use Outsider knowledge to build a believable setup story. Time the bonus kill after an Outsider death so it resembles another Demon or a Gossip outcome.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Golem
roles.ability: You may only nominate once per game. When you do, if the nominee is not the Demon, they die.
roles.play: Save your single nomination for a strong Demon candidate or a controlled death test. A non-Demon nominee dies immediately, which can bypass the ordinary vote plan.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Goon
roles.ability: Each night, the 1st player to choose you with their ability is drunk until dusk. You become their alignment.
roles.play: Track the first player who selects you each night because your alignment may change. Seek control over who acts first and do not assume your current team will remain your team.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Gossip
roles.ability: Each day, you may make a public statement. Tonight, if it was true, a player dies.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Gossip is due to kill a player, they die. :reminder:
roles.play: State one precise, falsifiable public claim each day and log it verbatim. Extra deaths may validate yesterday's gossip, but many other roles can create or prevent deaths.
roles.bluff: Make exact public statements and let existing extra deaths validate some of them. Do not retroactively change yesterday's wording.
roles.story: Record the exact public statement and evaluate it when the ability resolves. If true, choose a death that does not make the source mechanically certain.

roles.name: Grandmother
roles.ability: You start knowing a good player & their character. If the Demon kills them, you die too.
roles.firstNightReminder: Point to the grandchild player & show their character token.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the grandchild was killed by the Demon, the Grandmother dies too. :reminder:
roles.play: Find your grandchild privately and coordinate claims without making them an obvious target. If they die at night, your extra death is evidence but may also end your game.
roles.bluff: As evil, reproduce the role's timing, legal choices, and information format. Keep a written history and decide what event would make you reveal.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Gunslinger
roles.ability: Each day, after the 1st vote has been tallied, you may choose a player that voted: they die.
roles.play: Use the public kill threat to regulate suspicious voting. A shot gives immediate alignment pressure but can also remove a useful good voter.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Harlot
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a living player: if they agree, you learn their character, but you both might die.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Harlot chooses a living player. Put the Harlot to sleep. Wake the chosen player, show them the *THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU* token, then the Harlot token. If that player nods their head, wake the Harlot and show them the chosen player's character token. Both players might die. :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Choose a living player whose exact role is worth the death risk and obtain consent. A refusal is social information, not proof of alignment.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Imp
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. If you kill yourself this way, a Minion becomes the Imp.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Imp chooses a player. :reminder: If the Imp chose themselves: Replace 1 alive Minion token with a spare Imp token. Put the old Imp to sleep. Wake the new Imp. Show the *YOU ARE* token, then show the Imp token.
roles.play: Kill information engines and decide whether a star-pass improves the evil team's social position. Track Monk, Soldier, Ravenkeeper, Mayor, and Scarlet Woman explanations for unusual nights.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Give Demon information and three legal bluffs, process protection and poisoning before deaths, and check victory conditions after every death or character change.

roles.name: Innkeeper
roles.ability: Each night*, choose 2 players: they can't die tonight, but 1 is drunk until dusk.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Innkeeper chooses 2 players. :reminder: :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Protect two likely targets while choosing a pair where one player's drunkenness will not wreck the town. Tell the group enough afterward to explain unexpected information or survival.
roles.bluff: As evil, reproduce the role's timing, legal choices, and information format. Keep a written history and decide what event would make you reveal.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Investigator
roles.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Minion.
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the Minion character token. Point to both the *MINION* and *WRONG* players.
roles.play: Use the Minion type as well as the two names. Ask which candidate's behavior fits that Minion, but remember Spy and Recluse registration can distort the picture.
roles.bluff: Place a real Minion type between an expendable teammate and a good player. The claim becomes dangerous if the named Minion behavior cannot exist.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Judge
roles.ability: Once per game, if another player nominated, you may choose to force the current execution to pass or fail.
roles.play: Hold the ruling for a pivotal nomination. Forcing pass or fail can decide the game, so state the result and vote consequences unambiguously.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Juggler
roles.ability: On your 1st day, publicly guess up to 5 players' characters. That night, you learn how many you got correct.
roles.otherNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.play: Make up to five public guesses on day one and include enough real hypotheses to gain information. Keep the exact list and remember Vortox may force a false number.
roles.bluff: Make five day-one guesses and choose a result compatible with public claims. A zero can be safe but often looks evasive.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Klutz
roles.ability: When you learn that you died, publicly choose 1 alive player: if they are evil, your team loses.
roles.play: Before death, maintain a shortlist of safe living players. When you die, choose promptly and use alignment evidence rather than friendship or the loudest voice.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Librarian
roles.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Outsider. (Or that zero are in play.)
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the Outsider character token. Point to both the *OUTSIDER* and *WRONG* players.
roles.play: Check the expected Outsider count before treating the ping as simple confirmation. A zero is powerful; a two-player ping can locate the Drunk or expose an Outsider-count lie.
roles.bluff: Use a zero to support an unexpected setup, or point at an evil teammate and a real Outsider. Know the expected Outsider count before speaking.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Lunatic
roles.ability: You think you are a Demon, but you are not. The Demon knows who you are & who you choose at night.
roles.firstNightReminder: If there are 7 or more players, wake the Lunatic: Show the *THESE ARE YOUR MINIONS* token. Point to any players. Show the *THESE CHARACTERS ARE NOT IN PLAY* token. Show 3 good character tokens. Put the Lunatic to sleep. Wake the Demon. Show the *YOU ARE* info token and the Demon token. Show the *THIS PLAYER IS* info token and the Lunatic token, then point to the Lunatic.
roles.otherNightReminder: Do whatever needs to be done to simulate the Demon acting. Put the Lunatic to sleep. Wake the Demon. Show the Lunatic token & point to them, then their target(s).
roles.play: Act as the Demon you believe you are and watch for inconsistencies in kills, Minion contact, and bluffs. If the world breaks, pivot quickly and share your entire choice history.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Mastermind
roles.ability: If the Demon dies by execution (ending the game), play for 1 more day. If a player is then executed, their team loses.
roles.play: Preserve a believable good claim and prepare for the day after the Demon dies. The evil team needs town to execute again, so seed a convincing alternative Demon world beforehand.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Mathematician
roles.ability: Each night, you learn how many players’ abilities worked abnormally (since dawn) due to another character's ability.
roles.firstNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.otherNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.play: Record the number and identify which abilities could have malfunctioned because of another character. It counts abnormalities, not ordinary misinformation or failed guesses.
roles.bluff: As evil, reproduce the role's timing, legal choices, and information format. Keep a written history and decide what event would make you reveal.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Matron
roles.ability: Each day, you may choose up to 3 sets of 2 players to swap seats. Players may not leave their seats to talk in private.
roles.play: Rearrange seats to test neighbor abilities, disrupt evil coordination, or protect a vulnerable player. Explain moves clearly so information can be recalculated.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Mayor
roles.ability: If only 3 players live & no execution occurs, your team wins. If you die at night, another player might die instead.
roles.play: Build trust before final three and keep nominations disciplined. Night survival may be protection, a bounce, or simply a different Demon choice; do not overclaim confirmation.
roles.bluff: Survive toward final three and explain no-death nights as a bounce. The bluff becomes vulnerable if your voting and nominations do not resemble a good win condition.
roles.story: A Demon attack may bounce to another player, but only when the redirection makes a fair game. Track the three-alive no-execution win precisely.

roles.name: Minstrel
roles.ability: When a Minion dies by execution, all other players (except Travellers) are drunk until dusk tomorrow.
roles.play: Push executions on credible Minion candidates and announce the drunken day clearly if one dies. Use that day to reassess rather than trusting ability outcomes.
roles.bluff: After an executed teammate, attribute all strange information to the Minstrel day. Before that, the role can remain quiet and hard to test.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Monk
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player (not yourself): they are safe from the Demon tonight.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Monk chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Protect players likely to be attacked, not merely players who sound strongest. Repeatedly protecting the same player can test Demon choices but also reveals your pattern.
roles.bluff: Name protection targets after each night and use no-death nights as supporting evidence. Avoid claiming a target the real death pattern disproves.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Moonchild
roles.ability: When you learn that you died, publicly choose 1 alive player. Tonight, if it was a good player, they die.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Moonchild is due to kill a good player, they die. :reminder:
roles.play: Prepare a public target before death. Choose someone whose death would be useful if evil but whose loss is survivable if good.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Mutant
roles.ability: If you are “mad” about being an Outsider, you might be executed.
roles.play: Manage madness by sincerely presenting as Townsfolk when required. Coordinate carefully; fishing for confirmation or openly admitting the Outsider can invite execution.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Nightwatchman
roles.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a player: they learn you are the Nightwatchman.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Nightwatchman might choose a player. Put the Nightwatchman to sleep. Wake the target. Show the *THIS PLAYER IS* & Nightwatchman tokens, then point to the Nightwatchman. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Nightwatchman might choose a player. Put the Nightwatchman to sleep. Wake the target. Show the *THIS PLAYER IS* & Nightwatchman tokens, then point to the Nightwatchman. :reminder:
roles.play: Choose a player whose private confirmation can anchor a trust chain. Reveal only after comparing stories so evil cannot easily imitate the exchange.
roles.bluff: Coordinate with an evil teammate who can confirm receiving the signal. A lone unconfirmed claim has little mechanical weight.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: No Dashii
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Your 2 Townsfolk neighbors are poisoned.
roles.otherNightReminder: The No Dashii chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Seat-based poisoning is your shield and your tell. Kill players who can map the poisoned neighbors while maintaining a bluff compatible with their wrong information.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Give Demon information and three legal bluffs, process protection and poisoning before deaths, and check victory conditions after every death or character change.

roles.name: Ojo
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a character: they die. If they are not in play, the Storyteller chooses who dies.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Ojo chooses a character. :reminder:
roles.play: Name characters based on inferred claims. Choosing an out-of-play character hands the Storyteller the kill, which can be useful when you want ambiguity rather than precision.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: If the named character is absent, choose a fair death. Do not repeatedly punish the same team simply because the Ojo guesses poorly.

roles.name: Oracle
roles.ability: Each night*, you learn how many dead players are evil.
roles.otherNightReminder: Give a finger signal.
roles.play: Maintain a dead-player alignment table. Rising evil counts can reveal executed Minions, Fang Gu movement, or Vortox misinformation, but do not treat one number in isolation.
roles.bluff: Choose dead-evil counts that fit likely executed Minions and Fang Gu movement. A smooth sequence is easier to defend than arbitrary jumps.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Pacifist
roles.ability: Executed good players might not die.
roles.play: Advocate for valuable good players at the block without promising survival. Whether the Storyteller saves someone is discretionary, so read patterns cautiously.
roles.bluff: As evil, reproduce the role's timing, legal choices, and information format. Keep a written history and decide what event would make you reveal.
roles.story: Saving a good executee is discretionary. Use it sparingly enough that executions still carry information and players cannot reverse-engineer your generosity.

roles.name: Philosopher
roles.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a good character: gain that ability. If this character is in play, they are drunk.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Philosopher might choose a character. If necessary, swap their character token. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Philosopher might choose a character. If necessary, swap their character token. :reminder:
roles.play: Choose an ability that fills a gap in the current town and account for making an in-play holder drunk. Timing and public coordination are more important than raw power.
roles.bluff: As evil, reproduce the role's timing, legal choices, and information format. Keep a written history and decide what event would make you reveal.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Pit-Hag
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player & a character they become (if not in play). If a Demon is made, deaths tonight are arbitrary.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Pit-Hag chooses a player & a character. If they chose a character that is not in play: Put the Pit-Hag to sleep. Wake the target. Show the *YOU ARE* token & their new character token.
roles.play: Change characters to erase threats, create evil utility, or rewrite Demon identity. Expect arbitrary deaths when creating a Demon and track every setup-changing interaction.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Character creation can change setup counts. When a new Demon is created, use arbitrary deaths as needed to leave one viable Demon and a fair game.

roles.name: Po
roles.ability: Each night*, you may choose a player: they die. If your last choice was no-one, choose 3 players tonight.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Po may choose a player OR chooses 3 players if they chose no-one last night. :reminder: or :reminder: :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Sometimes choose nobody to threaten three deaths next night. A charge is strongest when the town cannot tell whether the quiet night came from you, protection, or drunkenness.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Give Demon information and three legal bluffs, process protection and poisoning before deaths, and check victory conditions after every death or character change.

roles.name: Poisoner
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned tonight and tomorrow day.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Poisoner chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Poisoner chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Target abilities whose failure creates a coherent wrong world. Change targets when useful, and sometimes allow true-looking information so the poisoning pattern is not obvious.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Politician
roles.ability: If you were the player most responsible for your team losing, you change alignment & win, even if dead.
roles.play: Help good sincerely unless a late, concrete route makes you most responsible for a loss. Vague disruption often loses with neither team crediting you.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Professor
roles.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a dead player: if they are a Townsfolk, they are resurrected.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Professor might choose a dead player. :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Resurrect a dead Townsfolk whose return gives both ability value and confirmation. Waiting can improve the target but risks dying with the ability unused.
roles.bluff: A dead evil teammate can return only through another mechanism, so this bluff is easiest while unused or after a real resurrection you can plausibly claim.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Pukka
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned. The previously poisoned player dies then becomes healthy.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Pukka chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Pukka chooses a player. :reminder: The previously poisoned player dies then becomes healthy. :reminder:
roles.play: Choose tonight's poison with tomorrow's delayed death in mind. Poisoned information before death is often more valuable than the kill itself.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Give Demon information and three legal bluffs, process protection and poisoning before deaths, and check victory conditions after every death or character change.

roles.name: Ravenkeeper
roles.ability: If you die at night, you are woken to choose a player: you learn their character.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Ravenkeeper died tonight, the Ravenkeeper chooses a player. Show that player's character token.
roles.play: Try to look valuable enough to kill without making the bait obvious. If killed, choose a player whose exact character will collapse several worlds, not just your loudest suspect.
roles.bluff: Act mildly kill-worthy, then explain survival as the Demon avoiding you. If executed, you never need to produce a result.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Recluse
roles.ability: You might register as evil & as a Minion or Demon, even if dead.
roles.play: Disclose early enough that registration explains pings, but do not let evil use you as a universal excuse. Volunteer for checks or execution when that separates worlds safely.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Registration is optional each time. Use it to create fair uncertainty, not to invalidate every correct conclusion or manufacture arbitrary losses.

roles.name: Sage
roles.ability: If the Demon kills you, you learn that it is 1 of 2 players.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Demon killed the Sage, wake the Sage and point to 2 players, 1 of which is the Demon.
roles.play: Look kill-worthy without becoming an obvious Sage bluff. If the Demon kills you, compare the two names against voting, nominations, and other information.
roles.bluff: Act valuable enough to be a plausible Demon target and, if killed by another cause, name two players including the preferred frame.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Sailor
roles.ability: Each night, choose an alive player: either you or they are drunk until dusk. You can't die.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Sailor chooses a living player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Sailor chooses a living player. :reminder:
roles.play: Choose players whose drunkenness can be tested with limited harm. Your survival is ambiguous, so combine it with repeated selections and other death-prevention claims.
roles.bluff: As evil, reproduce the role's timing, legal choices, and information format. Keep a written history and decide what event would make you reveal.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Saint
roles.ability: If you die by execution, your team loses.
roles.play: Stay useful and avoid becoming the default execution. A late claim is dangerous, but an immediate hard claim can hand evil an easy bluff; share selectively with trusted players.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Savant
roles.ability: Each day, you may visit the Storyteller to learn 2 things in private: 1 is true & 1 is false.
roles.play: Write both statements exactly and solve them across days as a constraint system. Ask the Storyteller to repeat wording; avoid deciding too early which half is true.
roles.bluff: Prepare two statements each day with one verifiably true fact and one false statement that pushes a useful world. The Storyteller will not supply your fake information.
roles.story: Prepare two statements daily with exactly one true and one false while sober. Make both relevant and comparably useful rather than one obvious throwaway.

roles.name: Scapegoat
roles.ability: If a player of your alignment is executed, you might be executed instead.
roles.play: Watch which alignment is under pressure because you may replace that execution. Your public advocacy should account for the Storyteller's option to redirect the result.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Scarlet Woman
roles.ability: If there are 5 or more players alive & the Demon dies, you become the Demon. (Travellers don't count.)
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Scarlet Woman became the Demon today, show them the *YOU ARE* token, then the Demon token.
roles.play: Stay credible and alive while five or more players remain. Be ready for the Imp to star-pass, and avoid tying your public story too closely to the original Demon.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Seamstress
roles.ability: Once per game, at night, choose 2 players (not yourself): you learn if they are the same alignment.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Seamstress might choose 2 players. Nod or shake your head. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Seamstress might choose 2 players. Nod or shake your head. :reminder:
roles.play: Use the comparison when it splits important worlds, often late. Pair a trusted anchor with a suspect rather than checking two unknowns with no follow-up plan.
roles.bluff: Name a pair and result that creates a useful alignment link. Waiting until late limits how many days town has to test it.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Shabaloth
roles.ability: Each night*, choose 2 players: they die. A dead player you chose last night might be regurgitated.
roles.otherNightReminder: A previously chosen player might be resurrected. :reminder: The Shabaloth chooses 2 players. :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Use two kills to pressure protection claims and choose whether regurgitation will create maximum uncertainty. Expect the town to compare every death and return against your pattern.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Each night choose two deaths, then optionally regurgitate a previously killed player on a later night. Returns should improve balance and mystery without feeling arbitrary.

roles.name: Slayer
roles.ability: Once per game, during the day, publicly choose a player: if they are the Demon, they die.
roles.play: Use the shot when its result will clarify worlds. A failed shot is not proof of goodness because you may be drunk, poisoned, or shooting a Recluse interaction incorrectly.
roles.bluff: Take a convincing shot at a good player or teammate and use failure as expected. Holding the shot too long makes the claim less testable.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Snake Charmer
roles.ability: Each night, choose an alive player: a chosen Demon swaps characters & alignments with you & is then poisoned.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Snake Charmer chooses a player. If they chose the Demon: Show the *YOU ARE* & Demon tokens. Give a thumbs down. Swap the Snake Charmer & Demon tokens. Put the old Snake Charmer to sleep. Wake the old Demon. Show the *YOU ARE* and Snake Charmer tokens & give a thumbs up. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Snake Charmer chooses a player. If they chose the Demon: Show the *YOU ARE* & Demon tokens. Give a thumbs down. Swap the Snake Charmer & Demon tokens. Put the old Snake Charmer to sleep. Wake the old Demon. Show the *YOU ARE* and Snake Charmer tokens & give a thumbs up. :reminder:
roles.play: Choose deliberately and keep a complete history. Hitting the Demon swaps your team and role, so prepare a credible public story for either side of the swap.
roles.bluff: As evil, reproduce the role's timing, legal choices, and information format. Keep a written history and decide what event would make you reveal.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Soldier
roles.ability: You are safe from the Demon.
roles.play: Invite a Demon attack by bluffing a strong information role, then reveal when a no-death night helps. Do not assume survival proves the Demon selected you.
roles.bluff: Use a no-death night as cover but do not insist it proves you. This bluff is strongest when you can explain why the Demon would attack you.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Spy
roles.ability: Each night, you see the Grimoire. You might register as good & as a Townsfolk or Outsider, even if dead.
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the Grimoire for as long as the Spy needs.
roles.otherNightReminder: Show the Grimoire for as long as the Spy needs.
roles.play: Use the Grimoire to construct a claim that fits real setup counts and private information. Feed the Demon targets, support teammates' stories, and exploit your ability to register as good.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Show the full Grimoire accurately and allow optional good/Townsfolk registration when an ability checks the Spy. Keep reminder tokens readable.

roles.name: Summoner
roles.ability: You get 3 bluffs. On the 3rd night, choose a player: they become an evil Demon of your choice. [No Demon]
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the *THESE CHARACTERS ARE NOT IN PLAY* token. Show 3 not-in-play good character tokens.
roles.otherNightReminder: Change the Summoner reminder token to the relevant night. :reminder: If it is night 3, the Summoner chooses a player & a Demon character. Put the Summoner to sleep. Wake the target. Show the *YOU ARE* and Demon tokens & give a thumbs-down.
roles.play: Survive through the third night, use the three bluffs to coordinate evil, and choose a socially trusted future Demon with a suitable Demon type. Plan how night-two deaths hide the missing Demon.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give three bluffs, omit the Demon from setup, and on night three process the chosen player and Demon. Before then, do not end the game merely because no Demon exists.

roles.name: Sweetheart
roles.ability: When you die, 1 player is drunk from now on.
roles.otherNightReminder: If the Sweetheart died, a player became drunk immediately. If you haven't done this yet, do so now. :reminder:
roles.play: Plan for the drunkenness your death creates. Tell trusted players enough that later contradictions can be attributed without publicly painting a target on yourself.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Make the drawback matter without turning the player into a spectator. Track any setup modification before tokens enter the bag.

roles.name: Tea Lady
roles.ability: If both your alive neighbors are good, they can't die.
roles.play: Coordinate neighboring executions and death tests. Your protection only applies when both living neighbors are good, so changes in survival narrow several alignments at once.
roles.bluff: Seat yourself between players you want trusted and use survival as evidence. Be prepared when either neighbor dies despite the claim.
roles.story: Re-evaluate both living neighbors whenever seats or alignments change. Protection is mechanical while the Tea Lady is sober and healthy.

roles.name: Thief
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself): their vote counts negatively tomorrow.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Thief chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Thief chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Choose a player whose negative vote will matter and make your alignment legible through the pattern. The target can still raise a hand, so track the arithmetic explicitly.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Tinker
roles.ability: You might die at any time.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Tinker might die. :reminder:
roles.play: Your death can occur at almost any fair moment, so use your voice before it does. Do not assign every unexplained death to a specific evil ability.
roles.bluff: As evil, make the claim fit the expected Outsider count and any setup modifiers. Explain why you hid or revealed without using the Outsider as a universal excuse.
roles.story: Choose a death moment that helps balance and creates a readable puzzle. Avoid arbitrary timing that erases a player's agency.

roles.name: Town Crier
roles.ability: Each night*, you learn if a Minion nominated today.
roles.otherNightReminder: Either nod or shake your head.
roles.play: Log every nomination and compare it with your result. Encourage controlled nomination patterns so a yes or no removes meaningful Minion worlds.
roles.bluff: Track Minion nominations and report a believable yes/no. Coordinate teammate nominations so your result never accidentally clears the entire evil team.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Undertaker
roles.ability: Each night*, you learn which character died by execution today.
roles.otherNightReminder: If a player was executed today, show their character token.
roles.play: Encourage informative executions, then keep your claim protected until you can reveal a chain. A result proves the executed character only if you were sober and healthy.
roles.bluff: Match public executions exactly and claim plausible roles. You can falsely confirm a teammate, but doing so ties both stories together.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Vigormortis
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Minions you kill keep their ability & poison 1 Townsfolk neighbor. [-1 Outsider]
roles.otherNightReminder: The Vigormortis chooses a player. :reminder: If that player is a Minion, poison a neighboring Townsfolk. :reminder: :reminder:
roles.play: Kill Minions when their dead abilities remain useful and use the resulting Townsfolk poisoning to corrupt a trusted chain. Make death patterns look accidental.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Give Demon information and three legal bluffs, process protection and poisoning before deaths, and check victory conditions after every death or character change.

roles.name: Village Idiot
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player: you learn their alignment. [+0 to +2 Village Idiots. 1 of the extras is drunk]
roles.firstNightReminder: If there are multiple Village Idiots, mark one as *DRUNK*. :reminder: Wake the Village Idiots one at a time to choose a player. Give a thumb signal.
roles.otherNightReminder: Wake the Village Idiots one at a time to choose a player. Give a thumb signal.
roles.play: Coordinate targets only after deciding whether multiple Village Idiots are plausible. Repeated alignment checks are strongest when they overlap, but one extra Idiot may be drunk.
roles.bluff: Keep a nightly target ledger and mix alignment results. Coordinate duplicate claims only if the script and setup plausibly support multiple Idiots.
roles.story: If adding extra Village Idiots, mark exactly one extra as drunk. Duplicate tokens are part of setup and should be accounted for before distribution.

roles.name: Virgin
roles.ability: The 1st time you are nominated, if the nominator is a Townsfolk, they are executed immediately.
roles.play: Arrange a nomination by a credible Townsfolk early enough that the confirmation matters. Do not waste the trigger on an Outsider claim or after the town has already committed elsewhere.
roles.bluff: Invite a Minion or Outsider teammate to nominate only if failure has a prepared drunkenness or non-Townsfolk explanation.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Vortox
roles.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Townsfolk abilities yield false info. Each day, if no-one is executed, evil wins.
roles.otherNightReminder: The Vortox chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Ensure all Townsfolk information is false and force an execution every day. Bluff around statements that can remain plausible under systematic falsity.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: All Townsfolk ability information must be false while sober and healthy. Track the daily execution requirement and distinguish information from rules or non-ability statements.

roles.name: Voudon
roles.ability: Only you & the dead can vote. They don't need a vote token to do so. A 50% majority isn't required.
roles.play: Dead players control the vote while you live, so organize them and watch for evil dead influence. Your exile immediately restores normal voting.
roles.bluff: Traveller identity is public. Bluffing concerns alignment: make your use of the ability look beneficial to the team you claim to support.
roles.story: Announce the public character, privately assign alignment, and use exile rather than execution rules. Keep the ability strong but legible.

roles.name: Washerwoman
roles.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Townsfolk.
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the Townsfolk character token. Point to both the *TOWNSFOLK* and *WRONG* players.
roles.play: Talk to both candidates separately before announcing the exact character. A quiet soft-confirmation can protect the real Townsfolk; later, compare whether either candidate's behavior fits the role.
roles.bluff: Prepare one real script Townsfolk as the shown character and place yourself or an ally in the pair. Keep the first-night wording and later role claim consistent.
roles.story: Resolve the ability in night order, record every choice and result, and preserve true information unless the player is drunk or poisoned or a rule explicitly changes it.

roles.name: Witch
roles.ability: Each night, choose a player: if they nominate tomorrow, they die. If just 3 players live, you lose this ability.
roles.firstNightReminder: The Witch chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.otherNightReminder: The Witch chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Curse likely nominators or create a trap around a public plan. Your bluff should explain why you are cautious about nominating without making the curse pattern obvious.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character, so focus on a separate good cover claim. If you are framing this Minion as in play, create more than one piece of supporting misinformation.
roles.story: Give Minion information correctly, track ongoing effects, and ensure misinformation remains attributable to legal causes rather than Storyteller invention.

roles.name: Yaggababble
roles.ability: You start knowing a secret phrase. For each time you said it publicly today, a player might die.
roles.firstNightReminder: Show the Yaggababble their secret phrase.
roles.otherNightReminder: For each time the Yaggababble said their phrase today, a player might die. :reminder:
roles.play: Use the phrase naturally and vary how many times it appears. Coordinate requested deaths with the Storyteller through public repetition without making the phrase identifiable.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: Write the phrase down, count public uses exactly, and choose no more deaths than uses. Deaths are optional; distribute them to create a fair, interpretable game.

roles.name: Zombuul
roles.ability: Each night*, if no-one died today, choose a player: they die. The 1st time you die, you live but register as dead.
roles.otherNightReminder: If no one died today, the Zombuul chooses a player. :reminder:
roles.play: Get executed while registering dead, then hide your continuing kills among Gossip, Tinker, and other causes. Avoid killing every night if doing so exposes that you remain alive.
roles.bluff: This is an evil character. Build a good cover that explains your survival and voting while using this Demon's visible pattern to support a different Demon world.
roles.story: On first death, mark the Zombuul as dead publicly but alive in the Grimoire. They kill only if nobody died during the day.

jinxes.reason: If the Cannibal gains the Butler ability, the Cannibal learns this.
If the Juggler guesses on their first day and dies by execution, tonight the living Cannibal learns how many guesses the Juggler got correct.
A Mastermind that has their ability keeps it if the Vigormortis dies.
The Chambermaid can detect if the Mathematician will wake tonight.
The Mathematician learns if the Drunk’s ability yielded false info or failed to work properly.
The Mathematician learns if the Lunatic attacks a different player than the real Demon attacked.
If a Pit-Hag creates a Damsel, the Storyteller chooses which player it is.
If the Pit-Hag turns an evil player into the Goon, they can't turn good due to their own ability.
If the Pit-Hag turns an evil player into the Politician, they can't turn good due to their own ability.
If there is a spare token, the Pit-Hag can create an extra Village Idiot. If so, the drunk Village Idiot might change.
The Recluse might register as the Demon to the Sage.
If there would be two Demons, one of which was the Scarlet Woman, the Scarlet Woman remains the Scarlet Woman.
If the Spy is (or has been) in play, the Damsel is poisoned.
The Summoner registers as the Demon to the Clockmaker.
If the living Summoner has no ability, the Storyteller has the Summoner ability.
If the Summoner creates a second living Demon, deaths tonight are arbitrary.
The Summoner may summon a Pukka on the 2nd night instead of the 3rd.
If the Summoner summons a dead player into the Zombuul, the Zombuul has already "died once".
If the Exorcist chooses the Yaggababble, the Yaggababble does not kill tonight.
